correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivative tests give the three conditional residual laws. Each residual is exactly a coordinate derivative, so conditional orthogonality yields the three variance defects. The recovery and adaptation regressions give the displayed covariance identities by one-line moment subtraction. Nonnegativity of \(x^2\) forces \(y\le c\) on stationary support. If any defect vanishes, the corresponding coordinate is constant along bounded complete support trajectories; the remaining stable linear filters or algebraic coordinate relations then force all coordinates constant, hence equilibrium support. The packaged checker independently verifies the residual, variance, and covariance algebra.

value.rationale: The Hindmarsh–Rose model separates neuronal activity into membrane voltage, fast recovery, and slow adaptation, and the literature interprets its bursting through slow-fast interaction between precisely those coordinates. The accepted theorem supplies a universal statistical calibration of that architecture: recovery is exactly anticorrelated with squared voltage, adaptation is exactly positively correlated with voltage, and the deviations from perfect correlation are equal to normalized mean-square coordinate speeds. These formulas apply to periodic bursting, chaotic bursting, and mixtures without requiring phase alignment or spike detection. They therefore provide exact consistency checks for long stationary traces and a distribution-level complement to the established bifurcation and slow-manifold descriptions.
